analysis: Examined test-only changes in the CI threat-review tooling. In .github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py (head 302-378, 431-498, 539-557), new tests cover several behaviors. Workload call policy admits only planned stages plus one shared repair slot, and an unplanned call is BudgetStopped (302-317). The emergency ceiling is 500 and the output-token cap is 16384 (319-334). The boto read timeout is 240s for fixed and 600s for workload, with no SDK retries (336-351). Workload planning stops at the ceiling (353-366). Invalid policy, ceiling or token values fail closed (368-377). Large-scan tests cover hierarchical integration (433-498). Incomplete final results require a human and forbid clearance (540-557). In .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py, the renamed test (664-671) now expects no OPUS local rescan after Sonnet integration uncertainty. It still requires manual_review_reasons, so uncertainty hands off to a human rather than clearing. New tests check that a manual rerun does no paid work and does not produce a clean result (949-959). They also check that scanner runtime is bounded to 60-3000s (961-967) and that the workload ceiling hands off at the integration planning stage (969-982). None of this touches the provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption or inference code described by the threat model (TB-002, TB-011 and others). The tests assert fail-closed CI merge gating and bounded spend; no product security regression is identified. Coverage limits: the implementation files behind these tests (threat_review/bedrock.py, budget_scan.py, merge_policy.py, the gate script and threat-model-review.py) are not in this batch. Integration should confirm that those implementations actually enforce what the tests assert. In particular: the removed OPUS depth pass must not let uncertainty clear without a human, and the raised ceilings (500 calls, 3000s) must remain bounded as configured in CI. These are review-tooling cost and availability concerns, not threat-model assets.
